t: A bag contains 3 red and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other without replacement. The probability that both are red is:
e: P(both red) = (3/5) × (2/4) = 6/20 = 0.30; the second draw is conditional on the first ball not being replaced.

t: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. Which statement is correct?
o: A and B are mutually exclusive
e: P(A)P(B) = 0.2 = P(A ∩ B), so A and B are independent; P(B|A) = 0.2/0.5 = 0.4 = P(B); P(A ∪ B) = 0.5 + 0.4 − 0.2 = 0.7.

t: Out of 1,000 independent lives aged 40 with q₄₀ = 0.003, the expected number of survivors at age 41 is:
e: Expected deaths = 1,000 × 0.003 = 3, so expected survivors = 1,000 − 3 = 997.

t: Two independent lives each have a one-year survival probability of 0.95. The probability that both survive the year is:
e: Under independence the probabilities multiply: 0.95 × 0.95 = 0.9025.

t: A prize scheme pays ₹1,000 with probability 0.1, ₹100 with probability 0.3 and nothing otherwise. The expected payout is:
The arithmetic mean of the first ten natural numbers (1 to 10) is:
e: The sum of 1 to 10 is 55, so the mean is 55/10 = 5.5.

t: A random variable has variance 0.0016. Its standard deviation is:
e: Standard deviation = √0.0016 = 0.04.

t: ₹1,00,000 is due in 10 years. Under a constant force of interest of 5% per annum (e^−0.5 = 0.6065), its present value is:

If the discount factor v = 0.95, the effective annual rate of interest is approximately:
e: i = 1/v − 1 = 1/0.95 − 1 = 1.0526 − 1 = 5.26%. The rate of discount here is d = 1 − v = 5%.

t: A perpetuity of ₹1,000 per annum has its first payment at the end of year 4. At 10% per annum (v³ = 0.7513), its present value is:
e: This is a 3-year deferred perpetuity: PV = v³ × (1,000/0.10) = 0.7513 × 10,000 = ₹7,513.

e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). a₄₀:₁₀ = (N₄₁ − N₅₁)/D₄₀ = (30,000 − 14,000)/2,000 = 8.

t: A project costs ₹10,000 today and returns ₹6,000 at the end of each of the next 2 years. At 10% (v = 0.9091, v² = 0.8264), its net present value is approximately:

e: Outstanding loan = PV of remaining instalments = 5,000 × 2.4869 ≈ ₹12,435.

e: A/E = 100/80 = 1.25 or 125%, meaning the experience is heavier than the standard table.

t: If pₓ = 0.99 and eₓ₊₁ = 30, the curtate expectation of life eₓ is approximately:
e: Using the recursion eₓ = pₓ(1 + eₓ₊₁) = 0.99 × 31 = 30.69.

t: For a whole life assurance of ₹1,000 with level annual premiums payable throughout life, Aₓ = 0.36 and äₓ = 12. The net annual premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Pₓ = Aₓ/äₓ = 0.36/12 = 0.03 per ₹1, i.e. ₹30 per ₹1,000 sum assured.

t: Assuming a uniform distribution of deaths within the year of age and qₓ = 0.04, the probability that a life aged x dies within the next six months is:
e: Under UDD, ₜqₓ = t × qₓ for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, so ₀.₅qₓ = 0.5 × 0.04 = 0.02.

t: Given Nₓ = 13,000 and Dₓ = 1,000, the whole life annuity-immediate aₓ is:
e: aₓ = Nₓ₊₁/Dₓ = (Nₓ − Dₓ)/Dₓ = (13,000 − 1,000)/1,000 = 12. Equivalently äₓ = 13 and aₓ = äₓ − 1.

t: Given N₆₅ = 5,000 and D₅₅ = 1,000, the value of a whole life annuity-due on a life aged 55 deferred 10 years, ₁₀|ä₅₅, is:
e: ₘ|äₓ = Nₓ₊ₘ/Dₓ = N₆₅/D₅₅ = 5,000/1,000 = 5.

Which statement about the whole life annuity value aₓ at a fixed rate of interest is correct?
o: it increases as the age x increases
it decreases as the age x increases
it equals the annuity-certain for the expectation of life
e: Fewer future payments are expected at higher ages, so aₓ falls as x rises. Valuing an annuity-certain over the expectation of life only approximates aₓ and overstates it.

t: For two lives, aₓ = 12, aᵧ = 10 and the joint life annuity aₓᵧ = 8. The last survivor annuity (payable while at least one is alive) is:
e: a over-bar xy = aₓ + aᵧ − aₓᵧ = 12 + 10 − 8 = 14.

t: For a life aged x, the n-year term assurance is 0.06 and the n-year deferred whole life assurance is 0.10 (both per ₹1). The whole life assurance Aₓ is:
e: A whole life assurance is the sum of cover for the first n years and cover thereafter: Aₓ = A¹ₓ:ₙ + ₙ|Aₓ = 0.06 + 0.10 = 0.16.

t: The control level of solvency ratio that every insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Available solvency margin must be at least 150% of the required solvency margin; falling below triggers IRDAI action.

e: Net single premium = 2,00,000 × 0.30 = ₹60,000.

t: A decreasing term assurance is most commonly used to:
o: cover the outstanding balance of a housing or other loan
e: The sum assured falls each year in line with the reducing loan balance, so the cover matches the outstanding debt at a low premium.

e: The annuity-immediate pays at ages x + 1 to x + n, so the numerator is Nₓ₊₁ − Nₓ₊ₙ₊₁; (Nₓ − Nₓ₊ₙ)/Dₓ is the annuity-due äₓ:ₙ.

t: The commutation function Sₓ = Nₓ + Nₓ₊₁ + Nₓ₊₂ + … is used mainly to value:
e: Sₓ is the second summation of Dₓ and gives the increasing annuity-due (Iä)ₓ = Sₓ/Dₓ, just as Rₓ gives increasing assurances.

t: If the net annual premium rate for a whole life assurance at age x is Pₓ = 0.02 per ₹1, the net annual premium for a sum assured of ₹2,00,000 is:
e: Net annual premium = 2,00,000 × 0.02 = ₹4,000.

t: Insurers generally charge slightly more in total when premiums are paid half-yearly or monthly rather than annually in advance, mainly because of:
o: loss of interest on the later instalments and extra collection expenses
the higher sum assured under such policies
e: Instalment premiums are received later than the annual premium, so the insurer loses interest, and each collection carries administrative cost; a frequency loading compensates for this.

t: The net annual premium for a policy is ₹30, with an initial expense of ₹100 incurred at outset and no other expenses. If äₓ:ₙ (the premium-paying annuity) = 10, the level gross annual premium is:
e: G × 10 = 30 × 10 + 100, so G = 400/10 = ₹40. The initial expense is spread over the expected premium payments.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 49% to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021; intermediaries may have 100%.
